key_insight: Variantscape combines NLP and large language models to extract literature-supported links among genetic variants, cancer types, and treatments at scale.
clinical_relevance: The tool may support precision oncology research and molecular tumour board preparation, but extracted associations are not treatment recommendations.
method: Screened biomedical abstracts for gene mentions.
Extracted and standardised variant–treatment–cancer associations using NLP and LLMs.
Checked associations against abstract text and assembled a literature-derived graph.
evidence_signal: Of 886,195 gene-containing articles, 37,895 (4.3%) mentioned all three entity types; LLM verification confirmed at least one association in 35,224 papers, yielding 44,644 verified graph edges.
watch_item: LLM verification against abstracts does not establish clinical validity; the abstract reports no independent expert-validation accuracy.
paper_title: Variantscape: Retrospective Study of Large Language Model-Based Extraction of Variant-Treatment-Cancer Associations from Published Oncology Abstracts
